findings.reason: `ExplicitSolveSeed` is defined as "an explicitly supplied total-flux state used as the solve seed" and its `resolve` returns that state unchanged, which is precisely seeding an edit from the previous terminal `ForwardEquilibrium.flux`; §5 should state the warm start is an `ExplicitSolveSeed` of the previous terminal flux and add no policy type, so an author does not author a parallel `WarmStartPolicy`.
findings.text: §5 demand (2) proposes a new "warm-start policy" ("Seed each edit from the previous edit's converged state rather than the cold portfolio") without naming the seed-policy seam that already does exactly this

findings.reason: §2 says "The default-wiring test landed by `solve-default-wiring` is rewritten", but a second module was created beside the owner, both landed on 2026-09-04 within 80 minutes (`384d759ec` created `tests/test_route_default_wiring.py`, 120 lines; `31ed5d2d5` created `tests/test_default_wiring.py`, 263 lines), so the "every production cell reads DEFAULT-ON" check can drift between them; the section should name `tests/test_default_wiring.py` as the single owner and fold the route wiring assertions in place. Census of the type, every instance with its site: `tests/test_route_default_wiring.py:31` and `tests/test_default_wiring.py:42` declare the same nine-field `REQUIRED_DEFAULTS` tuple by hand (`current_pin`, `settled_exit`, `own_mask_acceptance`, `continuation`, `best_iterate_retention`, `stagnation_stop`, `exact_kernels`, `cached_machine`, `compilation_cache`); `tests/test_route_default_wiring.py:44` and `tests/test_default_wiring.py:55` each define a near-identical `RecordingProfile`; `tests/test_route_default_wiring.py:61` and `tests/test_default_wiring.py:207` each expose a `production*_receipts` accessor over the same seven-or-more producers; `tests/test_route_default_wiring.py:103` and `tests/test_default_wiring.py:228` each parametrize a test over `REQUIRED_DEFAULTS` asserting every declared default resolved on; and `tests/test_route_seam_execution.py:103,120` asserts a third facet of the same contract — that a production route body passes its `ForwardSolveRequest` to the public solve and serializes `resolved_defaults` from the returned receipt — so that module should be named too, so the rewritten wiring test does not become a fourth owner.
findings.text: the plan's §2 default-wiring check has two owners that assert the same mechanism

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `nova/equilibrium/solve_request.py` (768 lines) hides the version-keyed default table, deviation computation, seed policies, pytree plumbing and receipt telemetry behind one small interface: build a `ForwardSolveRequest`, call `ForwardProfile.solve(request)`, read a `ForwardSolveReceipt`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2's default-wiring acceptance ("the wiring audit rerun reads DEFAULT-ON in every production cell") has two owners in the committed tree, `tests/test_default_wiring.py` and `tests/test_route_default_wiring.py`, both asserting the same mechanism with identical `REQUIRED_DEFAULTS`, `RecordingProfile` and `production_*_receipts` scaffolding.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — supplied counts public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; no section of this revision adds to any of the four families, so no section carries an unaccounted interface addition.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's design searches its own history well (the lede cites the capability-wiring audit and the 737-site budget-drift inventory; §5 cites `ForwardFluxOperator` as the holder of the raster target), but §5 proposes a "warm-start policy" without naming the seed-policy seam that already carries that capability in `nova/equilibrium/solve_request.py`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3's transport design extends rather than wraps: the coupling seam embeds the existing `ForwardSolveRequest` in `ForwardTransportInput` (`nova/transport/forward.py:208`) and derives `ForwardTransportReceipt.equilibrium_resolved_defaults` from the embedded request's policy (`_equilibrium_resolved_defaults`, `nova/transport/forward.py:342`) instead of re-declaring defaults; and §5's raster followup explicitly declines a new holder ("no new holder is needed").
